The expected output requires the agent to specifically discover and check the customer's own kernel log group (not under /aws/parallelcluster), identify per-node which stream carries kernel messages, and report per-node whether that stream was actually live across the entire window—clearly distinguishing 'no Xid found in a proven-live log' from 'not observable due to silence.' 

The agent's response does raise a caveat about compute_console_output and slurm_health_check streams having no new events (last entries Aug 26-27), which is a partial nod to the liveness concern. However, the agent never mentions discovering or checking a separate customer kernel log group outside /aws/parallelcluster namespace, and does not do a per-node breakdown of stream liveness across the 7 compute nodes. Instead, it treats the ~55K CloudWatch log group scan as the primary evidence and frames the overall conclusion as 'good evidence to point away from GPU hardware' despite acknowledging the raw kernel-message streams were silent for the entire window. This is essentially the anti-pattern the expected output warns against: reporting an absence of Xids as reassuring even though the stream that would carry kernel-level Xid codes was not live/proven during the window. The agent treats this as a minor caveat rather than a critical gap that should have prevented a confident 'no Xid or GPU hardware errors turned up' headline. The agent did not establish before answering whether kernel logging was actually arriving per node; it discovered the silence only as an aside after already concluding no errors were found.

Overall, the response fails to meet the specific standard of the expected output regarding rigorous verification of log liveness before concluding health, per-node granularity, and identification of a separate customer kernel log group.
